scope.full_target: For every prime p, every field K of characteristic p, every integer λ with 0≤λ<p, the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(C)-module V=V(λ) of dimension λ+1 with Chevalley generators x,y,h, every nonzero v∈V with xv=0 and hv=λv, and every arbitrary admissible lattice M⊂V (a free abelian subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under the integer enveloping subalgebra generated by all x^r/r!,y^r/r!), prove that V(K)=M⊗ℤK is nonzero and every K-linear subspace invariant under x,y,h is zero or V(K). Here L(K)=(ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗ℤK acts by the induced lattice operators, including the Chevalley construction in characteristic 2. No algebraic closure assumption on K is made, and λ=0 and p=2 are included.

hypotheses.statement: The characteristic of the field K is p.
V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(C)-module of highest weight λ, of complex dimension λ+1. The elements x,y,h are its Chevalley generators and satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y, [x,y]=h.

M is an admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup of V with an integer basis that is also a complex basis of V, and is stable under U_Z. It is arbitrary and is not required to be the minimal lattice.

source.statement: V(K) is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊂V(K), if W is invariant under the induced operators x,y,h, then W={0} or W=V(K). Thus V(K) is an irreducible L(K)-module, including λ=0 and p=2, over the given arbitrary field K.
